# FlutterGuard

> FlutterGuard is an Android app that audits Flutter APKs on the device. You pick an APK, it reads the release and reports what it finds, graded A, C or F as triage labels. It has no network access. MIT licensed. Android 8.0 and newer.

- Canonical: https://flutterguard.dev/
- Download: https://github.com/anasfik/FlutterGuard/releases/latest
- Source (MIT): https://github.com/anasfik/FlutterGuard
- Privacy: https://gwhyyy.com/privacy/flutterguard
- Contact: work@gwhyyy.com
- Issues: https://github.com/anasfik/FlutterGuard/issues
- Maintainer: Anas Fikhi, Flutter and Software Engineer

## What it reads

- Manifest and package data: permissions, exported components, SDK levels, ABIs, backup and debug flags
- Release contents: bundled SDKs, endpoints, hosts, keys and configuration that shipped in the APK
- libapp.so: strings and symbols inside AOT machine code
- Signing data: certificate identity and structural signature facts
- Route-like strings found in the binary

## Grades

A, C and F are triage labels attached to each check result. They tell you what to look at first. They are not a security certification.

## Offline by design

FlutterGuard requests no INTERNET permission. The APK you pick stays on the device, reports are kept in private app storage, and nothing is uploaded. No account, no root, no PC.

## Limits

- Static analysis is evidence, not proof
- No runtime hooking and no traffic interception
- libapp.so is AOT machine code: strings and symbols, not decompiled Dart
- Routes are candidate strings, not a navigation graph
- AABs are not supported; convert with bundletool first
- The signature check is structural
- Some ROMs block APK reads
- Scan only apps you own or have permission to test
- Uninstalling the app deletes private reports and history

## Legal

Use FlutterGuard only on applications you own or have permission to test. Findings are evidence for your own review, not an authorization to test third-party apps.

Full detail: https://flutterguard.dev/llms-full.txt
